national_framework: NITI Aayog Data Centre Evaluation Framework (Frontier Tech Hub, 14 October 2026)

documents.title: Data Centre Evaluation Framework to Help States Plan for Sustainable Growth
documents.description: Governing national framework establishing five evaluation pillars: Power and Energy, Water and Cooling, Siting and Environmental Sustainability, Economic and Strategic Value, and Policy/Governance. Mandates full-campus power ramp-up planning, peak-summer water balances, and milestone-linked approvals.

key_clauses.pillar_1_power: Joint developer/DISCOM/STU Power Readiness and Ramp-up Plan covering full planned campus load, substation headroom, feeder limits, and augmentation milestones. Deductions for renewable/storage count only with firm connectivity and usable capacity.
key_clauses.pillar_2_water: 20–30-year seasonal water balances based on peak-summer demand. Treated wastewater reuse must be physically contracted and connected before demand reduction is credited. Groundwater NOC required in stressed basins.
key_clauses.pillar_3_siting: Screening of candidate site polygons against 100-year flood lines, historical surface water presence, protected areas, and vulnerable settlements before statutory commitments.
key_clauses.pillar_4_economic: Assessment of compute readiness, AI/GPU enablement, and state fiscal incentives net of infrastructure costs.
key_clauses.pillar_5_governance: Single-window time-bound approvals with milestone monitoring and explicit tracking of missing vs verified evidence.

documents.title: Telangana Data Centres Policy
documents.issuing_authority: Information Technology, Electronics & Communications (ITE&C) Department, Government of Telangana
documents.description: Comprehensive state policy positioning Hyderabad as a premier data centre hub. Mandates dual power grid feeds, provides 100% stamp duty reimbursement, power tariff subsidies, green power open access, and TS-iPass single-window clearances.

key_clauses.power_provisions: Dual-grid feed from two independent substations by TSSPDCL/TSTRANSCO; 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years; power tariff subsidy of INR 1.00/unit for 3 years; open access for renewable energy with priority wheeling.
key_clauses.water_provisions: Industrial bulk water allocation via TSIIC and HMWSSB with dedicated pipeline connections; mandates rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling systems.
key_clauses.incentives: 100% reimbursement of stamp duty and transfer duty on land purchase or lease; capital subsidy up to 20% of investment in IT equipment for MSME edge centres; patent and certification support.
key_clauses.clearances: Time-bound clearances via TS-iPass within 21 days; deemed approval provisions for building plan and power connections.

documents.title: Maharashtra New Information Technology and Information Technology Enabled Services (IT/ITES) Policy - 2023
documents.issuing_authority: Industries, Energy and Labour Department, Government of Maharashtra
documents.description: State industrial resolution granting data centres 'Essential Services' status (ESMA). Details stamp duty exemptions (100% in Zone B/C/D, 75% in Zone A), electricity duty exemptions for 10-20 years, power tariff subsidies, additional FSI up to 4.0, and MAHITI portal single window clearance.

key_clauses.power_provisions: Electricity duty exemption for 10 to 20 years depending on the location zone; power tariff subsidy of INR 1.00 to INR 2.00 per unit for 3 years; green energy tariff incentives; dual HT feeder lines via MSETCL/MSEDCL.
key_clauses.water_provisions: Assured industrial water allocation from MIDC and CIDCO at industrial bulk tariffs; mandate for zero liquid discharge (ZLD) and tertiary treated water for cooling systems.
key_clauses.incentives: 100% stamp duty waiver in non-congested zones (Pune/Chakan/Talegaon and Nagpur); additional Floor Space Index (FSI) up to 3.0 in municipal areas and 4.0 in MIDC parks without premium; relaxation of floor-to-ceiling heights up to 6 meters.
key_clauses.clearances: MAHITI single-window portal with 30-day time-bound statutory clearances; essential services classification ensuring 24x7x365 uninterrupted operations.

documents.title: Karnataka Data Centre Policy 2022–2027
documents.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
documents.description: Establishes Karnataka as a premier data destination targeting 200+ MW capacity additions. Defines eligible Data Centre Units (min 3 MW IT load) and Data Centre Parks (min 20 MW IT load), capital subsidies outside Bengaluru Urban, 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years, and FAR up to 4.0.

key_clauses.power_provisions: 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years; power tariff concession of INR 1.00/unit for 3 years; dedicated substation rights and dual-feeder provision from KPTCL/BESCOM; open access renewable energy banking.
key_clauses.water_provisions: KIADB and BWSSB bulk allocation; mandates treated effluent recycling and rainwater harvesting integration.
key_clauses.incentives: Capital subsidy of up to 10% on fixed capital investment outside Bengaluru Urban (max INR 10 Crore); 100% stamp duty exemption on land purchase/lease; Floor Area Ratio (FAR) up to 4.0 in KIADB industrial areas.
key_clauses.clearances: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) facilitation; time-bound clearance via Karnataka Single Window Portal.

documents.title: Operational Guidelines for Karnataka Data Centre Policy 2022
documents.issuing_authority: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
documents.description: 131 pages of exhaustive administrative procedure, verification checklists, application forms, and sanction criteria for obtaining data centre incentives, building plan approvals, and power connections in Karnataka.

key_clauses.verification_rules: Detailed checklists for verifying IT load, commissioning milestones, power connectivity sanctions, and land title clearances before incentive disbursement.
key_clauses.audit_trail: Prescribes statutory audit certificates and PUE benchmarking thresholds required for annual subsidy release.

documents.title: Tamil Nadu Data Centre Policy 2021
documents.issuing_authority: Information Technology Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
documents.description: State policy leveraging Chennai's undersea cable landings to attract hyperscale data centres. Minimum threshold: 3 MW IT load or INR 500 Crore investment. Provides dual HT power feeds via TANTRANSCO, stamp duty concessions, and building height flexibilities. Note: Policy text specifies applicability through 31 March 2026, requiring active renewal verification.

key_clauses.power_provisions: Dual HT feeder connectivity from two separate 230 kV / 110 kV substations by TANTRANSCO/TANGEDCO; green energy wheeling with concessional cross-subsidy surcharge; 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years.
key_clauses.water_provisions: SIPCOT piped industrial water and CMWSSB tertiary treated reverse osmosis (TTRO) recycled water supply prioritized for cooling towers.
key_clauses.incentives: 100% stamp duty exemption in Category B & C districts, 50% in Category A (Chennai/Chengalpattu); building height relaxation and higher FSI under Tamil Nadu Combined Development and Building Rules (TNCDBR).
key_clauses.validity_note: Clause 3 specifies policy operative until 31 March 2026. Developers must verify active extension notifications for projects commissioning beyond 2026.

documents.title: CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector - User Guide (Version 22.0)
documents.issuing_authority: Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Ministry of Power, Government of India
issuing_ministries: CEA Clean Energy & Energy Transition Division
documents.description: The definitive, peer-reviewed statutory emission factors for the Indian electricity grid for FY 2025-26. Used for computing Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, carbon usage effectiveness (CUE), and displacement by renewable energy additions.

key_clauses.national_factors: Weighted Average Grid Emission Factor: 0.675 tCO2/MWh; Operating Margin (OM): 0.963 tCO2/MWh; Build Margin (BM): 0.446 tCO2/MWh; Combined Margin (CM 50:50): 0.705 tCO2/MWh.
key_clauses.regional_factors: Southern Regional Grid (Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu): 0.698 tCO2/MWh; Western Regional Grid (Maharashtra): 0.742 tCO2/MWh.
key_clauses.generation_mix: Accounts for 310.58 BU of renewable energy generation out of 1,761.28 BU total net electricity generation.

documents.title: CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector - Raw Database Workbook (Version 22.0)
documents.issuing_authority: Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Ministry of Power, Government of India
documents.description: Station-by-station and unit-by-unit fuel consumption, thermal efficiency, gross generation, auxiliary consumption, and CO2 emissions for every grid-connected generator in India.

key_clauses.data_scope: Covers thermal, hydro, nuclear, and grid-scale renewable generating units across all states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Telangana.

documents.title: Government Open Data License - India (GODL) Gazette Notification
documents.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
documents.description: Establishes the legal framework for open data reuse, adaptation, value addition, and commercial redistribution for datasets published on data.gov.in and government departmental portals.

key_clauses.license_terms: Grants worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use, adapt, and distribute data subject to explicit attribution and avoidance of misleading representation.

documents.title: Uttar Pradesh Data Centre Policy 2026 - Official Notification
documents.issuing_authority: Department of IT & Electronics / Invest UP, Government of Uttar Pradesh
documents.description: Official 2026 notification distinguishing Data Centre Parks (min 30 MW), Data Centre Units (min 5 MW), and Edge Data Centres. Outlines AI compute booster and land rebates.

key_clauses.categories: Parks (min 30 MW IT load), Units (min 5 MW IT load), Edge Centres (< 5 MW); interest subsidies up to INR 50 Cr; capital subsidy up to INR 20 Cr; land rebates up to 50% in Bundelkhand/Purvanchal.

documents.title: Odisha State Data Center Policy 2022
documents.issuing_authority: Electronics & Information Technology Department, Government of Odisha
documents.description: Policy framework for positioning Bhubaneswar and coastal Odisha as disaster-resilient eastern data hubs with submarine landing points.

key_clauses.incentives: 100% exemption on electricity duty for 10 years; land allotment via IDCO; single-window clearance through GO SWIFT.
